ranges.name: Aberdare Range
ranges.description: A 160 km upland range in central Kenya, north of Nairobi, averaging about 3,500 m; its Kikuyu name is Nyandarua.
ranges.formation_note: Part of the eastern rim of the Great Rift Valley, falling steeply into the rift on its western side.

ranges.name: Adrar des Ifoghas
ranges.description: A massif in Mali’s Kidal Region reaching into Algeria, with wide, shallow valleys strewn with eroded granite blocks.

ranges.name: Aïr Mountains
ranges.description: A triangular massif in northern Niger, within the Sahara, rising above 1,800 m.
ranges.formation_note: Its volcanic features include the extinct Arakao caldera, lava flows, volcanic cones and one of the largest ring-dike systems in the world.

ranges.name: Anti-Atlas
ranges.description: A range in southern Morocco running about 500 km north-east from the Atlantic towards Ouarzazate and Tafilalt, bordering the Sahara.

ranges.name: Auas Mountains
ranges.description: Namibia’s highest range, 56 km long near Windhoek; Moltkeblick is its highest peak.

ranges.name: Bale Mountains
ranges.description: Mountains in south-east Ethiopia, part of the Ethiopian Highlands, with Tullu Demtu, the country’s fourth-highest peak, and the Sanetti Plateau, home of the Ethiopian wolf.

ranges.name: Cameroon Line
ranges.description: A 1,600 km chain of volcanoes from islands in the Gulf of Guinea through Mount Cameroon towards Lake Chad.
ranges.formation_note: Unusual in crossing both ocean and continental crust; geologists have proposed several explanations for it.

ranges.name: Crater Highlands
ranges.description: Volcanic highlands along the East African Rift in northern Tanzania, named for their many craters and calderas, Ngorongoro among them.
ranges.formation_note: Several large volcanic complexes, about 2.4 to 1.5 million years old, built where the African and Somali plates spread apart.

ranges.name: Drakensberg
ranges.description: The eastern part of the Great Escarpment around southern Africa’s central plateau, stretching more than 1,000 km and highest on the Lesotho–South Africa border.
ranges.formation_note: Steep rift walls formed when southern Gondwana broke apart, since eroded inland; the high Drakensberg is capped by basalt that erupted about 180 million years ago.

ranges.name: Ethiopian Highlands
ranges.description: The largest continuous area of high ground in Africa, sometimes called the “Roof of Africa”; the East African Rift cuts across it.
ranges.formation_note: A dome of ancient rock lifted by magma from the mantle from about 75 million years ago, then capped by flood basalts from about 30 million years ago.

ranges.name: Fouta Djallon
ranges.description: A highland region in central Guinea, roughly the area of Middle Guinea.

ranges.name: High Atlas
ranges.description: The highest part of the Atlas Mountains, running east from the Atlantic across central Morocco to the Algerian border; Jbel Toubkal is its highest peak.
ranges.formation_note: Folded and uplifted when old rift basins were squeezed as Africa and Eurasia converged during the Cenozoic.

ranges.name: Hoggar Mountains
ranges.description: A highland region in the central Sahara in southern Algeria; Mount Tahat is Algeria’s highest peak.
ranges.formation_note: Mostly metamorphic rock about 2 billion years old, with younger volcanic rock in places.

ranges.name: Imatong Mountains
ranges.description: Mountains in south-eastern South Sudan reaching into Uganda; Mount Kinyeti is the highest point of South Sudan.
ranges.formation_note: Ancient crystalline basement rock rising through the younger deposits of the surrounding plains.

ranges.name: Kipengere Range
ranges.description: A plateau-like ridge in south-west Tanzania at the northern end of Lake Nyasa, also called the Livingstone Mountains, known for its flower-rich montane grasslands.
ranges.formation_note: Ancient Precambrian rock forming part of the eastern escarpment of the East African Rift.

ranges.name: Maloti Mountains
ranges.description: The mountains of Lesotho’s highlands, part of the Drakensberg system: a high alpine basalt plateau rising to Thabana Ntlenyana, southern Africa’s highest peak.

ranges.name: Marrah Mountains (Jebel Marra)
ranges.description: A massif of volcanic peaks in Darfur, the highest mountains in Sudan; Deriba Caldera is the highest point.

ranges.name: Middle Atlas
ranges.description: The northernmost and second-highest of Morocco’s three main Atlas chains, a mass about 350 km long that includes the volcanic cone of Jbel Hebri.

ranges.name: Mitumba Mountains
ranges.description: Mountains along the Western Rift Valley in the eastern DR Congo, west of Lakes Tanganyika and Kivu; the northern part is known as the Itombwe Mountains.
ranges.formation_note: Its two main peaks, Mount Kahuzi and Mount Biéga, are dormant volcanoes.

ranges.name: Rif
ranges.description: A mountain region in northern Morocco between the Mediterranean, the Atlantic and the Ouergha and Moulouya rivers.
ranges.formation_note: Geologically part of the Gibraltar Arc (the Alborán Sea region).

ranges.name: Rwenzori Mountains
ranges.description: A range on the border of Uganda and the DR Congo whose upper slopes are permanently snow-capped and glaciated; its streams feed one of the sources of the Nile.
ranges.formation_note: An uplifted block of ancient crystalline rock raised about three million years ago: not volcanic, and not formed by a collision of plates.

ranges.name: Saharan Atlas
ranges.description: A sub-range of the Atlas, mainly in Algeria with its eastern end in Tunisia, parallel to the Tell Atlas nearer the coast; Mount Issa is its highest peak.
ranges.formation_note: Ancient base rock covered by the sediments of shallow seas and rivers.

ranges.name: Semien Mountains
ranges.description: Plateaus cut by deep valleys and rising to pinnacles in northern Ethiopia, part of the Ethiopian Highlands and a World Heritage Site; Ras Dashen is Ethiopia’s highest mountain.
ranges.formation_note: Basalt lava some 3,000 m thick laid over ancient crystalline rock, formed in the same way as South Africa’s Drakensberg.

ranges.name: Tell Atlas
ranges.description: An Atlas chain over 1,500 km long, mainly across northern Algeria, forming a barrier between the Mediterranean and the Sahara; Lalla Khedidja is its highest summit.

ranges.name: Tibesti Mountains
ranges.description: A range in the central Sahara, mostly in the far north of Chad; Emi Koussi is the highest point of both Chad and the Sahara.
ranges.formation_note: Lifted over a mantle plume; its central third is volcanic, built by a hotspot active from the Oligocene, in places into the Holocene.

ranges.name: Togo Mountains
ranges.description: A range across central Togo that continues into Ghana as the Akwapim Hills and into Benin as the Atakora Mountains, averaging about 700 m.

ranges.name: Virunga Mountains
ranges.description: A chain of eight major volcanoes where Rwanda, the DR Congo and Uganda meet; Karisimbi is the highest.
ranges.formation_note: Volcanoes of the Albertine Rift, beside the western branch of the East African Rift; most are dormant, but Nyiragongo and Nyamuragira are active.
